name: Westbridge
region_detail: Western bank of the lower Storbruhn at the Great Eastway crossing, upstream from the river mouth and the northern shore of Lake Ophar.
site_type: settlement | Inhabited locations | River port and commercial town; administrative seat of the Marquisate of Westbridge.
history: A pre-Edict Cadorian trading post developed beside a landing and a timber bridge crossing the western river channel to a low island. The West Bridge gave the town its name. Ferrymen and merchants maintained customary navigation and trade arrangements with neighboring peoples. Cedric Bellamy selected the settlement as his seat following the Edict of the East in 3E-991.
current_state: In 3E-992 the town is a principal junction of road and river commerce. Bellamy regulates shipping through his town customs offices and holds a separate royal concession over the Western Customs House (L-WB-007) at the western outlet of Lake Ophar into Cador. His proposed fortified station near the mouth of the Storbruhn would extend control over inland frontier traffic and is contested by the Namaris and other river peoples. The existing Old Span and proposed bridge improvements are subjects of commercial and political debate.
inhabitants: Merchants, boatmen, dockworkers, ferrymen, dwarven Emberhearth craftspeople, officials, River Spurs, and visiting Ssaresh, Thalenweald, Namaris, and Qasari traders.
danger_level: Low ordinarily in established districts; localized waterfront crime, smuggling, flooding, and disputes. Shipping outside town may face piracy and contested navigation.
points_of_interest:
Lower Quays; Factors’ Row; Old Bridge and Old Span; Emberhearth district and foundries; Riverside; Bellamy Heights and River Spurs headquarters; town Customs House; Ironmark Assay & Trust; Overland Yard; Lantern Deck; Dockside Refuge; sheriff’s office. The Western Customs House (L-WB-007) is a separate installation.

Unresolved elements: Exact map hex; local street plan and building layouts; opening job and rumor selections; the extent of future bridge tolls and construction of the proposed Storbruhn station.
discovery: Western bank of the lower Storbruhn at the Great Eastway crossing, upstream from the river mouth and the northern shore of Lake Ophar. The Great Eastway, Storbruhn, and Lake Ophar connect Westbridge to Cador, the interior frontier, and southern caravan roads.
